newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Hume plays down talk of going for Irish presidency.
newsitem.headline: Hume plays down talk of going for Irish presidency.

text.p: Northern Irish peace broker John Hume played down speculation on Thursday that he might succeed Mary Robinson as president of Ireland.

A leading Dublin bookmaker chain had tipped moderate nationalist leader Hume as favourite after Robinson announced on Wednesday she would not seek a second term when her seven-year term expires in December.
Former prime minister Albert Reynolds was second favourite at 5/1 and poet Seamus Heaney, a Nobel literature prize-winner, was put at 12/1.
But Hume told Irish radio he had not been consulted and was putting his energy into trying to achieve an end to decades of sectarian strife in British-ruled Northern Ireland.
"I am concentrating on the job that I have," said Hume, who leads the province's Catholic Irish nationalist SDLP."I have heard this speculation but nobody has ever talked to me about it.

"But I have to be honest, I am concentrating on the job I am in public life to do, which is to do everything in my power, together with my colleagues, to bring about lasting peace and lasting stability in (Northern Ireland)."

Last year Irish Republican Army guerrillas ditched a 17 month ceasefire in fight against British rule. The province's 60 per cent Protestants support the British link but Catholics want an all-Ireland state under Dublin.

Social Democratic and Labour Party chief Hume is on a trip to the United States and will have talks with President Clinton later Thursday or on Friday about the deadlocked Northern Ireland peace process.
He put proposals to Britain late last year which he believes would have broken a deadlock and achieved an IRA ceasefire.
Britain turned down the proposals, which arose from talks between Hume and Gerry Adams, head of the IRA's Sinn Fein political arm.
Although Hume holds one of Northern Ireland's 17 seats in the British parliament he is eligible in Irish law to stand for the presidency of the south.
The Irish Republic, which gained independence after partition in 1922, extends citizenship to many people in Northern Ireland.
Robinson, a former lawyer widely acclaimed for bringing a new vibrancy to her non-party political role, said on Wednesday she wanted to devote herself to human rights activities.
Irish media have speculated that she might be in the running for a position at the United Nations.
